_note: Sixteen curated generation seeds, chosen off a 48-seed parity sweep on 2026-09-16 for the Industrialisation phase; four replaced off a re-sweep on main 2026-09-17 (NR-887).

A SEED IS THE SAVE. Generation is a pure function of the world descriptor, so a seed reproduces its world exactly on a given binary; there is no separate snapshot format and none is needed. What a seed cannot carry is why it was chosen, which is what this store holds.

THE FINGERPRINT IS NOT A GOLDEN. It is five counters from seed_library_sweep.json at the repo root, and a world-moving item is SUPPOSED to move them. Re-read with `node tools/session/seed_library.js --check` after such an item, and `--bless` once the movement is authorised. The rationale is the part that survives; the numbers are there so a future session can tell whether the world it generates is still the world described.
THE POOL WAS SWEPT AT PARITY (BL-1007): scripts/world_gen.lua and scripts/works.lua, the shipped data layer. Readings taken before 2026-09-16 describe a different world and do not compare.

To check or bless, regenerate the library's own table first: `build_gen/verify/exploration_sweep.exe --seeds $(node tools/session/seed_library.js --seed-list) --out seed_library_sweep.json` (BL-1026). The checked-in exploration_sweep.json carries seeds 0..15 only and is not the library's table.

A `review` field marks a seed whose rationale is under Ben's review in NEEDS_REVIEW, naming the entry and the candidates; it is removed when he rules. A `replaces` field records which seed an entry took the place of, and why.

READINGS AND RATIONALE REWRITTEN 2026-10-07 (Ben's ruling, after the sprint 49 re-bless) from seed_library_sweep.json at main c77f2d5a, with haulage from docs/development/drafts/sprint-49-rebless.md. The lake cap (BL-1200) redrew every world. Rankings in the `why` lines are against the other fifteen library seeds, not the 48-seed curation pool, which has not been re-swept.

pool.config: scripts/world_gen.lua + scripts/works.lua (21 works rows), main at 4c9feb4c

seeds.name: The rich world
seeds.why: The richest world in the library by a wide margin: a median polity chest of 3.67M against a next-best of 9,519 (seed 41), the largest top chest at 594M, 36 post roads (the most; the next is seed 40's 10) and 5 subjects, tied for the most. If firms cannot form here they cannot form anywhere, so it is the ceiling case for chartering.

seeds.name: The quiet world
seeds.why: The floor of the political map: 41 polities and 666 corridors, both the fewest in the library, 33 flows (second fewest), two post roads, no subjects and a 156 median chest. Its trade is no longer the floor: volume 7,374 sits mid-library and seed 12 now carries the fewest flows and the lowest volume. First-year haulage, 1,423.5 units sold at destination, is the second lowest of the sixteen. Industrialisation has to produce something legible from few polities and a thin network here.
seeds.replaces: seed 17 (Ben, 2026-09-17, NR-887: the old seed no longer answered this question)

seeds.name: The crowded world
seeds.why: The most crowded: 115 living polities and 28,371 Empire battles, both the most in the library, with 97 flows, the highest flow volume (14,584) and 249 standing treaties. Its median chest is 197 and its top chest, 38.7M, is the smallest of the sixteen. Many poor traders rather than a few rich ones: the hardest case for a firm that needs a treasury behind it.

seeds.name: The trade-dense world
seeds.why: The busiest network in the library: 99 flows (tied with seed 25 for the most) across 105 polities, 3,303 corridors and 290 standing treaties (both the most), with displacement at 40.7. The best world to watch prices form on, because there is already something moving.

seeds.name: The second road world
seeds.why: Ten post roads, the second most in the library after seed 46, with a 479 median chest and 43 flows. It no longer stays home: 1,108 frontier battles against 15 neighbour wars, displacement 73.9, the second highest of the sixteen. The case it was chosen for, money and infrastructure without an outward turn, it no longer answers; seed 12 is now the library's only held world.
seeds.replaces: seed 6 (Ben, 2026-09-17, NR-887: the old seed no longer answered this question)

seeds.name: The most inward world
seeds.why: The inward extreme, and the only HELD seed in the library: 116 neighbour wars against 24 frontier battles (displacement 0.21). It has the fewest flows (22), the lowest volume (3,418), the fewest standing treaties (48) and the fewest Empire battles (4,982), with one subject and a 120 median chest. Whatever the phase does here, it does with almost no outward turn, colonial ties or capital. The lake cap barely touched it (Empires battles 4,983 -> 4,982), so it is also the control for that change.

seeds.name: The frontier world
seeds.why: Displacement 57.9 (1,216 frontier battles against 21 neighbour wars) with one subject alive of five subjections formed: the conflict moved outward and almost nobody stayed subjected. A near test that trade relationships can form without an overlord graph to inherit; seeds 28, 31, 43 and 25 now carry zero subjects. It also has no post road against 77 flows, the cleanest roadless trade in the library.

seeds.name: The colonial world
seeds.why: Fifty-six subjections formed through Exploration, the second most after seed 0's 78, and 53 of them freed: only two subjects are alive at 1660. A colonial age that mostly came undone, in a world of 81 polities and 87 flows at displacement 7.27. The preferred-seller ties EXPLORATION hands forward survive here in two subjects only; seeds 46 and 38, with five each, now carry the most living ties.

seeds.name: The quiet Exploration world
seeds.why: Forty-seven Exploration battles, the fewest in the library by a wide margin (the next is seed 12's 140), against 8,657 in Empires. Almost all of them are frontier (46 against one neighbour war). The median chest is 9,519, the second highest of the sixteen, and one subject is alive. It no longer answers the question it was chosen for, colonial ties without capital: both halves have reversed.

seeds.name: The small poor world
seeds.why: Forty-six polities, a 105 median chest (the lowest in the library) and no subjects, none ever formed. Its first-year haulage, 1,412.9 units sold at destination on 284 convoys, is the lowest of the sixteen. It no longer answers the question it was chosen for, concentrated wealth in a thin political map: the wealth is gone.

seeds.name: The neighbour-war world
seeds.why: 510 neighbour wars, the most in the library (seed 11 is next at 300), against 617 frontier battles: displacement 1.21, the lowest of the fifteen displaced seeds. On most other axes it is middling: 77 polities, 55 flows, 9,574 volume, 5 post roads and a 182 median chest. It no longer answers the question it was chosen for, roads without traffic or capital: its post roads fell to the library middle and its first-year haulage rose from 138.9 to 2,247.1 units.

seeds.name: The one-road traders
seeds.why: One post road, 65 flows and the highest first-year haulage in the library: 2,943.6 units sold at destination, on 819 convoys. Trade that barely bought a road. Seed 37, with 77 flows and no post road, is now the cleaner roadless case, and seed 32 is no longer the paved mirror it was chosen against.

seeds.name: The big busy world
seeds.why: 24,258 Empire battles, 84 polities, 99 flows (tied for the most) and 13,808 volume: large, violent and commercial at once. It also dispatches the most convoys in the library in its first play year (869). The stress case for whatever Industrialisation runs per polity per round.

seeds.name: The small colonial world
seeds.why: Forty-seven polities holding five subjects, tied with seed 46 for the most, with no post road, 34 flows and a 303 median chest. Displacement is 56.1 (505 frontier battles against 9 neighbour wars). It no longer answers the question it was chosen for, wealth that stayed home: the median chest is 303, not the 8.6M it read when curated, and the conflict turned outward.
seeds.replaces: seed 19 (Ben, 2026-09-17, NR-887: the old seed no longer answered this question)

seeds.name: The few-neighbour frontier
seeds.why: A frontier world with almost no neighbour wars: 297 frontier battles against 6, displacement 49.5, with 3 subjects, 50 polities, 40 flows and a 157 median chest. It no longer tests the displacement reading itself: with six neighbour wars the ratio is defined, and no library seed now reads displaced(no-nb).
seeds.replaces: seed 4 (Ben, 2026-09-17, NR-887: the old seed no longer answered this question)

seeds.name: The reference world
seeds.why: Seed 0 is the descriptor default and the world every harness, capture and golden is written about; the wizard board capture of 2026-09-16 was taken on this seed. It belongs here because a library needs the world everything else is compared against, not because it is unusual. On this binary it is not ordinary on every axis: its displacement, 147.1, is the highest in the library, and its 78 subjections formed are the most.
